title: Rigidity of morphisms of finite locally constant sheaves
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient setting $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ of [def-pur-conventions] and [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $T$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $k$-scheme and let $L,M$ be finite locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules: they are locally constant in the sense of [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] and have finite underlying sets at every geometric stalk [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk].

1. The ordinary internal Hom sheaf $\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_T}(L,M)$ of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] is finite locally constant on $T$.
2. If a morphism $\varphi:L\to M$ vanishes at one geometric point of every connected component of $T$, then $\varphi=0$. In particular, if $T$ is connected, two morphisms $L\to M$ which agree at one geometric point agree everywhere.

Here Hom and morphisms are taken in the ordinary category of module sheaves, rather than the derived category; the other coefficient versions in the purity conventions are the separately specified coefficient transports. A connected component means a maximal connected subset of the underlying topological space.

proof.text: Restrict intrinsic module sheaves to the constant scalar ring. Use the proved localConstancy_iff, finite_stalk_iff and finiteLocal_iff helpers of Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtaleIntrinsicLisseFixed (import all). These compare intrinsic local constancy and finite geometric module stalks with fixed-scalar finite constant models. Their coefficient comparison is the locally bijective module sheafification unit. Finiteness of the positive-level coefficient ring is Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing.

Take the fiber-product common refinement of the two fixed-module model covers. Pro-etale covers are stable under base change and composition. Pullback along each weakly etale projection preserves constant sheaves by continuous sheafification compatibility. The localization equivalence identifies pullback models with models on the slice site. This is commonFiniteModels in the Lean proof; the constantSheafOverIso restriction comparison retains the constant values.

Internal Hom commutes with restriction to a slice: use the existing PresheafOfModules.restrictOverHomObjIso and the fully faithful forgetful functor on module sheaves. The fixed-module constant model lifts uniquely to the intrinsic ringed-module constant model, because restriction along the locally surjective constant scalar unit is fully faithful. A finite module over a finite ring is finitely presented (Module.finitePresentation_of_finite). The constant internal-Hom comparison therefore identifies the local Hom with the constant module of linear maps. This module is finite by the injection into the finite set of functions between the two finite model values.

The finite Hom models prove local constancy. For each geometric point lift its terminal fiber element through the covering using the proved point construction of Sheaf.Paper.ProEtaleFiniteModelStalks (import all). Its slice fiber is the original fiber, by the cofinal over-category comparison sheafFiberOverIso. The fiber of a constant sheaf is its value. Hence the Hom stalk is finite. Transport back using finite_stalk_iff. This proves clause (1), including empty bases and empty covering members.

For clause (2), etale_origin_of_finite_models gives finite locally constant etale origins L0 and M0 with comparison isomorphisms. Fullness of comparisonUpperStar gives f0 whose inverse image is eL.hom followed by f followed by eM.inv. The natural colimit-forgetful isomorphism carries the assumed zero intrinsic stalk map to the zero fixed-scalar stalk map; naturality of proEtale_comparison_stalk then gives zero etale stalk map for f0 at the prescribed point of each connected component. Apply the already proved AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.eq_zero_of_sheafFiber_map_eq_zero in WeilConjectures.ConstructibleSheaf.Rigidity, the etale realization of the rigidity clause of this same blueprint node. Its proof takes the locally constant image of f0, uses its clopen stalk-zero locus and connectedness to prove that image zero, and hence f0 zero. Map this equality through comparison and cancel the origin isomorphisms; faithfulness of constant-scalar restriction gives f = 0.

On a connected scheme every connected component is the whole space. For two maps agreeing at the specified geometric point, use that point in every component and apply clause (2) to their difference. The actual geometricRingModuleStalkFunctor is additive, so its map of the difference is zero. Subtraction then gives equality of the maps.
